items.label: NextEra Energy press release: NextEra Energy, U.S. Department of Commerce and Government (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: NextEra Energy executed definitive agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Government of Japan

set.signal: NextEra Energy executed definitive agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Government of Japan to fund the development and operation of up to 10 gigawatts of natural gas-powered generation in Texas and Pennsylvania. Development activities include down payments on long-lead equipment, including turbines, and selection of EPC contractors. Initial resources are expected to come online as early as the end of 2028, with the projects expected to be completed in 2032, subject to permitting, regulatory requirements and completion of development, construction and commissioning. CEO: the Texas and Pennsylvania projects are two of the over 30 energy hubs in various stages of development in the portfolio.
set.figure: definitive agreements executed; up to 10 gigawatts of gas-fired generation (Texas and Pennsylvania); initial resources as early as end of 2028; completion expected 2032

items.reason: Japan's $550 billion U.S. investment commitment is a government/trade-deal figure, not NextEra's, and the funding-tranche release is a financing term (§2); operating facts kept unchanged.
items.evidence: which were selected in connection with Japan's $550 billion investment commitment to the United States ... This major milestone releases the first tranche of funding for the two projects

items.label: NuScale Power press release: NuScale Power and MillenniTEK Advance Manufacturing (09-01-2026)
items.signal_prefix: NuScale and MillenniTEK, an advanced nuclear materials manufacturer, fabricated first-of-a-kind

set.signal: NuScale and MillenniTEK, an advanced nuclear materials manufacturer, fabricated boron-oxide pellets (described by the companies as first-of-a-kind) for NuScale's passive emergency core cooling system (ECCS); the pellets are designed to dissolve into the reactor coolant on ECCS actuation to control core reactivity without operator intervention. CEO: working with manufacturers like MillenniTEK progresses 'the production-ready processes needed to support our first customer deployments'. A manufacturing-process milestone, not a stated production order.

items.reason: 'First-of-a-kind' is the company's claim and must be attributed (§2.4); source also says the pellets are 'designed to' dissolve.
items.evidence: today announced that they have successfully fabricated first-of-a-kind boron-oxide pellets ... the pellets are designed to dissolve into the reactor coolant
